ui_bugs.issue: Locking from inside an open chat STILL bounces the user to ChatLockGate. Even though `unlockedKeys` is now a useState set in /app/frontend/src/chat-settings.tsx (lines 77, 134-143) and `markUnlocked(threadId)` IS called inside submitLock at /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:749 right before `await reload()`, the next render still evaluates `alreadyUnlocked = wpSettings.isUnlocked(threadId) || unlockedThisSession` as FALSE. Result: the ChatLockGate at line 213-218 mounts and the profile modal + composer are unmounted. Screenshot proof: /app/test_reports/iter19_screenshots/06c_after_lock.png. Backend correctly persisted the lock (verified via GET /api/chat/settings -> locked_thread_ids=['4f3c5028-...']). Reference: /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:208-221 and /app/frontend/src/chat-settings.tsx:134-143.

integration_issues.issue: PATCH /api/chat/lock/threads returns 200, GET /api/chat/settings confirms the lock persists, BUT the UI bounces to <ChatLockGate>. The iteration-19 fix (state-ifying unlockedKeys) did not solve it. Recommended next step: ALSO pass `onLocked={() => setUnlockedThisSession(true)}` from ChatThreadScreen → ProfilePrivacyBlockRows and call it inside submitLock right before reload(). This way the gate's check at line 209 (`isUnlocked(threadId) || unlockedThisSession`) sees the local state-flag flipped immediately on the SAME render that flips `locked` to true, removing any reliance on context-memoization timing.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): Lock-from-inside still bounces to ChatLockGate. The unlockedKeys-as-state change in /app/frontend/src/chat-settings.tsx is NOT enough. Add an `onLocked` callback prop to ProfilePrivacyBlockRows. In ChatThreadScreen (line ~483-487 where the component is rendered), pass `onLocked={() => setUnlockedThisSession(true)}`. Inside submitLock at /app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:749, call `onLocked?.()` immediately AFTER the PATCH succeeds and BEFORE `await reload()`. This guarantees the gate's check at line 209 (`isUnlocked(threadId) || unlockedThisSession`) returns true on the very same render that flips `locked` to true via the reload-driven settings update — no reliance on cross-state ordering.

FIX (MEDIUM): Add testID='login-submit' to the Sign-in TouchableOpacity in the login screen so testing agents can reliably tap it without relying on text matching (which is failing in playwright on RN-Web for this button).

After both fixes land, retest steps: (1) Login as Alice via UI; (2) Navigate to thread 4f3c5028-...; (3) Tap header → open profile; (4) Tap 'Lock this chat' → enter 1234 → tap Confirm; expect: PATCH 200, modal closes (sheet=null), profile modal stays open, row label flips to 'Chat locked', composer + messages still visible, NO ChatLockGate. (5) Close profile → navigate /chat (tab) → tap thread → expect ChatLockGate appears (cold navigate forgets unlock). (6) Enter 1234 at gate → unlocks → conversation visible. (7) Reopen profile → tap 'Block Bob' → confirm → row flips to 'Unblock Bob'. (8) Tap again → confirm → flips back. (9) Tap 'Wallpaper' → navigates to /chat/settings.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/chat-settings.tsx:77 — useState<Set<string>>(new Set()) — note the initializer `new Set()` is called on every render but useState ignores it after first mount. Functionally fine but consider `useState<Set<string>>(() => new Set())` to skip the wasted allocation. Not the cause of the bug.
/app/frontend/src/chat-settings.tsx:134-141 — markUnlocked uses the function form of setUnlockedKeys with an early-return-same-reference when the key is already present. Correct.
/app/frontend/src/chat-settings.tsx:142 — `isUnlocked = useCallback(..., [unlockedKeys])` — correctly memoized on the state. Correct.

/app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:209 — `const alreadyUnlocked = wpSettings.isUnlocked(threadId) || unlockedThisSession;` — both branches should be checked. The fact that the gate STILL appears after submitLock proves that AT THE RENDER WHEN `locked` becomes true, `isUnlocked(threadId)` returns false. Possible explanations: (a) React 18 batches both setStates and reads unlockedKeys via the new closure but the closure captured an older Set instance, (b) the provider's useMemo dep array allows a render where settings already updated but isUnlocked still references the older state — unlikely with hook semantics but worth verifying. The DEFINITIVE fix is to also bump `unlockedThisSession` in the child (via the onLocked prop) so the OR branch trips regardless of context-memoization timing.

/app/frontend/app/chat/[id].tsx:741-755 (submitLock) — markUnlocked(threadId) is correctly called before await reload(). The issue is that this only updates context state; the local `unlockedThisSession` in ChatThreadScreen is not touched. Adding the onLocked prop is the cleanest patch.

rca_of_issue: PRIMARY: ChatThreadScreen renders ChatLockGate when `locked && !alreadyUnlocked`. After submitLock awaits the PATCH, calls markUnlocked(threadId), and awaits reload(), the very next render has BOTH `locked=true` (from reload's setSettings) AND `isUnlocked(threadId)` SHOULD be true (from markUnlocked's setUnlockedKeys). In theory the gate guard should pass. In practice the gate renders — empirically verified by screenshot 06c_after_lock.png. Most likely root cause: React 18 batches setUnlockedKeys and setSettings such that the first paint sees settings updated but the isUnlocked closure captured by the new context value still references the prior unlockedKeys Set (subtle hook-closure-order interaction with useMemo on the context value). The CLEAN mitigation is to ALSO set `unlockedThisSession` in ChatThreadScreen via an onLocked callback prop — since unlockedThisSession is a local useState in the SAME component that owns the gate guard, React schedules its update in the same priority as the consumer's render, eliminating the ordering bug. Reproduction: clean state (has_pin=true, locked_thread_ids=[]), enter /chat/<threadId>, tap header, tap Lock, enter PIN 1234, tap Confirm — observe immediate bounce to gate instead of staying in the chat with row flipped to 'Chat locked'. Mitigation: see action_items #1.
